title: upgrade attention kernels: flashattnv2 + fused-ops + rope/rotary optimizations + scheduling
author: Asha Patel
release_notes: Performance: Upgrade attention kernels to FlashAttentionV2 with fused QKV and rotary/rope optimizations. Improves throughput and tail latency for common LLMs. Behavioral: no functional changes; runtime falls back to previous kernels when unsupported. Ops: new scheduling knobs for continuous batching and KV prefetching.
description: Motivation: Upgrade the inference runtime's attention implementation to FlashAttentionV2 (and our in-house variants) with fused ops and optimized application of rotary/rope embeddings. This change targets long-tail production latency and unit-cost improvements for customer workloads that have long context windows and high concurrency. The PR includes: fused QKV kernels, fused rotary application to avoid extra memory passes, compact KV cache layout with optional prefetching, and scheduler improvements to incorporate kernel cost models for continuous batching. Backwards compatibility: when a model shape/hardware configuration is not supported by the optimized kernel, we automatically fall back to the existing attention path.
commits: feat(kernels): add FlashAttentionV2 wrapper and kernel selection logic
perf(attn): implement fused QKV + rotary fused op path
refactor(kv): compact KV cache layout + prefetch hooks
sched: integrate kernel cost model into continuous batching decision path
tests: add microbenchmarks and correctness tests for fused kernels
ci: add flashattnv2 nightly perf job and GPU matrix
diff_summary: Added optimized kernels and schedulers (new .cu/.cpp files) + tests and docs. Small changes to model loader to annotate supported kernel capabilities. No changes to public API. Approx +2.4k additions, -812 deletions.
review_comments: Miguel Torres: Nice work — can you add a short note in the scheduler docs about the new cost model inputs? Also requested a small test for CPU fallback.
Author (Asha): added scheduler docs and CPU fallback unit test in a follow-up commit (see commits).

Lina Zhang: Bench numbers look promising; please run p50/p99 for the 8k context experiment and include GPU memory usage. Found a small correctness edge-case with rotary for odd head dim; fixed in commit.
Ben Carlson: Minor nits on naming and logging; requested adding a feature flag to toggle the compact KV format for staged rollout — implemented behind runtime flag.
CI: initial GPU matrix failed on older CUDA image due to compile flags; resolved by conditional defines and re-run — all checks passed on final run.
performance_summary: +18-28% throughput on Llama-like 7B/13B for generation with 2048-8192 context; tail latency (p99) reduced ~10% on high-concurrency workloads. KV memory footprint reduced ~12% with compact layout. Continuous batching throughput improved by 15% for mixed short/long workloads after kernel cost model integration.
compatibility_notes: Runtime maintains automatic fallback to existing attention kernels if FlashAttentionV2 variants are not supported on target hardware or model config. Added runtime flag 'enable_compact_kv' for staged rollout.
test_plan: Unit tests for fused ops and rope application under tests/attn_unit, microbenchmarks under tests/attn_perf. Nightly perf job added to CI matrix. Manual verification on Dedicated cluster (p4d and a100 fleets) and canary rollout to 5% traffic for one week.
merge_summary: Merged by squash on 2024-11-07 after approvals from Miguel, Lina, and Ben. Merge strategy: squash and merge. All CI checks green. Canary rollout scheduled post-merge.
post_merge_actions: Monitor: p50/p95/p99 latency and GPU memory usage dashboards
If regression: toggle 'enable_compact_kv' runtime flag and rollback kernel selection
notes: This PR is part of ENG-5120 (attention kernel modernization) and ENG-5246 (continuous batching scheduler improvements). Follow-ups: refine kernel cost model with live telemetry and extend fused ops to additional attention variants.
